summary.headline: Surya Roshni Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33% YoY to ₹2,448 crore, but EBITDA grew only 1% to ₹143 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 33% YoY and 20% QoQ to ₹2,448 crore, with PAT up 3% YoY to ₹77 crore. Steel pipes and strips drove the top line with 35% revenue growth to ₹1,941 crore, while EBITDA per ton stayed well below the earlier guidance at around ₹4,105 per ton. Lighting and consumer durables grew 16-17% in revenue, with management guiding to a stronger H2. The company remains debt-free with a cash surplus of ₹75 crore. Management reiterated FY27 targets and set longer-term goals for FY28 and FY30.

segments.name: Steel pipes and strips
segments.commentary: Q2 volume was a record, up 22% YoY in H1 to about 4.96 lakh tons with revenue up 35% to ₹3,531 crore in H1. EBITDA per ton was ₹4,105 in Q2 versus ₹4,006 in Q1 and ₹5,013 in Q2 FY26, and the order book is about ₹1,200 crore.

segments.name: Lighting and consumer durables
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue was ₹507 crore (+17% YoY) and H1 revenue was ₹964 crore (+16%). Management said EBITDA would have been ₹48 crore without a ₹3.5 crore EPR charge and higher advertising spend, and the professional lighting order book is about ₹200 crore.

guidance_outlook: Lighting and consumer durables: FY27 guidance of 22-23% value growth and about 25% volume growth; beyond FY27, about 20% value growth in FY28 and about 15% CAGR through FY30 with EBITDA margin of about 9-9.5%.
Steel pipes: expects about 6 lakh tons volume in H2 FY27 after about 5 lakh tons in H1, and about 14 lakh tons in FY28 at EBITDA of ₹4,600-4,800 per ton.
Steel EBITDA per ton: management expects about ₹4,800-4,900 in H2 and about ₹5,000 in Q4, calling ₹5,000 the new normal.
Management said it remains on track for FY27 targets and expects a stronger H2 for both businesses, citing festive and year-end demand.
Management indicated a share buyback proposal may come before the next board meeting, but gave no details.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of about ₹150 crore, with ₹50 crore for an existing-plant expansion expected to be commissioned by May 2027.
Next year's capex includes about ₹75 crore for a phase 2 expansion.

Greenfield plant of about 3-3.5 lakh tons capacity, investment of about ₹250-300 crore, targeted at value-added products with ₹4,000-7,000 per ton margin; site identified near a port in the east, with approvals and land being pursued over the next 2-3 months.
Total steel pipe capacity to exceed 2 million tons after the greenfield additions.
demand_pricing: Steel pipe volumes benefited from rising steel prices; import of about 60,000 tons of raw material was booked at higher prices, with short-term margin impact.

API pipe demand softened as coating material costs rose; the average tender size fell from about 10,000 to 8,000 tons, with pressure expected to ease in 2-3 months. Domestic API order book rose by about 20,000 tons.
Indian section and square pipe segments were said to be growing 18-20%, with overall Indian pipe industry growth of 10-12%.
Lighting faces price erosion and pressure from unorganized players; management said most rivals are struggling to reach double-digit growth.
Lighting's strengths cited as nationwide distribution and pre-booking of imported material ahead of price increases; the company has increased wire and cable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the steel division's EBITDA per ton of about ₹4,500 now the new normal, versus earlier guidance of over ₹5,500?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was about ₹4,000 per ton and H2 is expected at ₹4,800-4,900, with ₹5,000 per ton in Q4 as the new normal, aided by price pass-through in exports, API and trade.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 volume outlook for steel pipes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 5 lakh tons delivered in H1 and about 6 lakh tons expected in H2, targeting about 11-14 lakh tons in future years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the increase mainly to freight and advertising, partly offset by lower administrative expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for API pipes in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said city gas and cross-country tenders are reviving, with a booking of about 20,000 tons, but average tender size fell from 10,000 to 8,000 tons due to coating material costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lighting EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will be better, with a longer-term target of about 9% EBITDA margin and double digits possible in more than a year, given market uncertainty.

risks_watch: Steel EBITDA per ton, which was about ₹4,000 in H1 against earlier guidance of over ₹5,500; management's ₹4,800-4,900 H2 target needs to be tracked.
Rising steel and coating material costs and the API tender slowdown could weigh on volumes and margins.
Lighting margin pressure from price erosion, unorganized competition, and rising advertising and freight costs.
Execution of the greenfield plant and commissioning timelines in the coming quarters.
Shareholder questions on the buyback and dividend, and the lack of a formal announcement.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and H2 visibility and stated its targets with specific numbers, but was evasive on the steel EBITDA per ton shortfall and on the buyback, which it deferred to the next board meeting. Several answers were unclear or contradictory, and the call transcript is partly garbled, so some figures should be verified against the filing.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 lighting value growth of 22-23% and steel volume of ~11 lakh tons (5 lakh H1 + 6 lakh H2), backed by a ~₹1,200 crore steel order book and ~₹200 crore lighting professional order book, plus a greenfield 3-3.5 lakh t plant (₹250-300 crore) still only at site-identification stage and a ₹50 crore expansion due May 2027; steel EBITDA/ton guidance was cut to ~₹4,500-4,600 for

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Steel EBITDA per ton was ~₹4,105 in Q2 vs ₹5,013 in Q2 FY26, with management guiding ₹4,800-4,900 in H2 and ~₹5,000 in Q4, but the FY27 implied level is cut to ~₹4,500-4,600 and the H2 ramp is unproven.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (₹50 cr expansion); greenfield later
rows.why: ₹50 crore existing-plant expansion due by May 2027 (Q4 FY27) and a greenfield 3-3.5 lakh t plant (₹250-300 crore) still at site-identification with approvals over the next 2-3 months, so commissioning falls beyond the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated ~6 lakh t steel volume in H2 after ~5 lakh t in H1 (H1 volume +22% YoY), plus lighting ~25% volume growth guided for FY27, backed by a ~₹1,200 crore steel order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex ~₹150 crore is committed, with ₹75 crore phase 2 planned next year and the ₹250-300 crore greenfield plant site already identified, so further capex news is firmly on the agenda.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Steel EBITDA/ton guidance was cut from over ₹5,500 to ~₹4,500-4,600 for FY27, and H1 EBITDA was only +18% YoY, so a raise is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA grew only 1% YoY to ₹143 crore on steel EBITDA/ton of ₹4,105 vs ₹5,013 a year ago, and H2 needs a ~₹4,800-4,900 ramp plus API tender sizes falling from 10,000 to 8,000 tons.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Greenfield plant targets value-added products at ₹4,000-7,000 per ton margin, but timing is not firm and it is only at site-identification; lighting launches were not specified.

rows.label: Steel order book ~₹1,200 cr; lighting pro order book ~₹200 cr
rows.why: Steel order book of about ₹1,200 crore and lighting professional order book of about ₹200 crore support the H2 volume ramp, though API tender sizes fell from 10,000 to 8,000 tons.

rows.label: Share buyback proposal
rows.why: Management indicated a buyback proposal may come before the next board meeting but gave no size or details, so it is not yet firm.

rows.label: Steel price pass-through and import cost headwind
rows.why: About 60,000 tons of raw material imported at higher prices carries a short-term margin hit, while API pressure from coating costs is expected to ease in 2-3 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 volume, lighting FY27 guidance and the greenfield plan, but evasive on the steel EBITDA/ton shortfall versus earlier guidance and deferred the buyback to the next board meeting; analysts pushed on the ₹4,500 'new normal' and the H2 margin ramp.
